My immediate thought was to trace the network of interconnected rooms and corridors. I systematically mapped out each room's approximate location and the configuration of the connecting corridors.

I moved left from the start room (T4). I mapped out the horizontal and vertical connections, paying close attention to any directional changes or potential obstacles. I meticulously traced each corridor, noting any "jog" or "step" configurations within them. The goal was to establish a clear, unobstructed path. I needed to ensure that the route was a continuous chain and did not contain dead ends.

I then followed the chain: from T4, it goes to T3, then to T2 (making note of the vertical connection T2-M2), and then M2-M3. After M3 it proceeds to M4, and from M4 it continues to B4. B4 then links up to B3, which goes to B2, and finally B2 goes into B1, where the goal chest is found.

I then performed a pixel-by-pixel inspection, carefully noting coordinates for start, goal, and all room centers and corridor segments. I measured each "jog" and directional change inside each corridor, taking note of its exact x and y coordinate. I had to make sure the measurements were accurate and verified against the image's overall pixel dimensions (approximately 978px wide, 818px tall).

I meticulously re-traced the path, adding the coordinates for corridor bends to generate a detailed list of points along the solution, from Start to Goal. I verified that all horizontal/vertical coordinate changes were accurate, checking to see if the path stayed within the room boundaries for the open corridor segments, and finally verified that all steps/jogs were identified and accurate. Finally, I used the most accurate measurements and verified that the path followed corridor centers.

After all this, I'm confident that the identified path is accurate, unobstructed, and efficient. I have the detailed route and key coordinates ready.
